I use **O1–O8** for the eight numbered items in `ORACLE_BRIEF.md`.

### 1. Secant-variety condenser for low-weight mixed powers
**Core/expected move.** Parameterize the affine fiber as \(x=x_0+Gu\), take its degree-\(r\) Veronese lift, then apply an explicit rank condenser injective only on secant varieties generated by at most \(S\) lifted points. If every dangerously light mixed word has secant rank \(\le S\), this could retain powered distance with \(O(Skr)\), rather than \(\sum_{i\le r}\binom{k}{i}\), coordinates.

**Map check.** O1: global degree \(r\), outside only when \(r\) exceeds available cubes. O2: no marginals/tableaux. O3: no scopes; odd holonomy remains an explicit threat. O4: no phases. O5: binary algebraic lift, not an integer exact-fiber slack. O6: uses affine generators, not complete-assignment columns, though generator computation may hide exponential expansion. O7: genuinely code-dependent dense folding; arbitrary mixed words are covered only if the secant-rank lemma holds. O8: binary output transfers exactly; rank is the condenser output dimension.

**Falsification/experiment.** For \(q=3,m=8,r=3,4\), enumerate every lifted mixed word, compute minimum secant rank, and search a condenser preserving all words below weight 25. Include all-eight and holonomy codes.

**Likely death.** Minimum NO words have unbounded secant rank, or constructing the projected generator requires the full Veronese basis.

---

### 2. Polarized affine-coset shortening
**Core/expected move.** After each reduced tensor square, canonically order coordinates and apply a dense Möbius/Arıkan transform \(P=F_2^{\otimes s}\); then delete transformed coordinates that vanish identically on the star-zero subcode. The hope is that matching fibers polarize into a few sparse channels while odd-cover fibers retain many active channels, giving exact code-dependent compression rather than puncturing raw coordinates.

**Map check.** O1: no local signatures. O2: no wire or marginal interfaces. O3: global transform sees the entire code, although odd holonomy may polarize just as well. O4: no phase labels. O5: no integer repair variables. O6: computed from \(H,t\), not assignments. O7: outside ordinary puncturing/type merging because coordinates are first densely mixed; every mixed tensor word must still be checked. O8: the resulting binary matrix transfers exactly; output rank and worst YES weight are explicit.

**Falsification/experiment.** Apply canonical polar transforms of sizes \(8,16,64\) to the existing reduced-square YES/NO, all-eight, affine-closure, and holonomy suites; exhaust every transformed word before shortening.

**Likely death.** No transformed coordinate becomes identically zero, or polarization densifies YES minima more than NO minima.

---

### 3. Rank-metric sandwich with support-sensitive inner blocks
**Core/expected move.** Regard a reduced-square word as a matrix \(W\), apply a deterministic family \(A_sWB_s\) of lossless rank condensers, and encode each surviving row-space direction by a simplex/BCH block. Unlike the killed five-block \(F_8\) condenser, include diagonal support probes so the claimed lower bound is “rank times surviving base support,” not merely nonzeroness.

**Map check.** O1: global bilinear sketches, not bounded local views. O2: no tableau communication. O3: no scopes, but holonomy can create low-rank matrices. O4: no phases. O5: entirely binary linear. O6: labels derive from the generator/parity-check matrix, not assignments. O7: this is a code-dependent asymmetric fold; soundness must quantify over every mixed \(W\), not only pure squares. O8: simplex blocks are binary-linear, so exact CVP transfer applies; their YES baseline must be counted.

**Falsification/experiment.** On \(q=3,m=8\), enumerate every mixed \(W\), record \((\operatorname{rank}W,\) row/column support\()\), and test Gabidulin-style \(A_s,B_s\) plus diagonal probes. Require hostile illegal costs above worst YES and improved rank exponent.

**Likely death.** Pure NO squares remain rank one, while inner blocks reproduce the prior YES-baseline inflation.

### 4. Splitter-sparse Magnus/Fox jet lift
**Core/expected move.** Assign free-group generators to global incidence cycles and attach a truncated Magnus expansion together with first and second Fox derivatives. Retain only monomials isolated by an explicit splitter family; derivative jets are intended to detect the all-eight and holonomy words whose ordinary Schur-walk features vanish identically.

**Map check.** O1: only outside the cube theorem when truncation degree grows beyond the hostile cube dimension; fixed degree is covered. O2: direct global ANF coefficients avoid multiplication tableaux. O3: cycles are global rather than proper scopes, directly targeting holonomy. O4: multi-valued nilpotent jets are not copy-stable scalar phases. O5: no integer slack fibers. O6: polynomially many cycle monomials, not complete assignments—conditional on a sparse hitting family. O7: not tensor amplification; all mixed jet words still require enumeration/proof. O8: coefficients over \(F_2\) give an exact binary transfer with rank equal to retained jets.

**Falsification/experiment.** Degree three or four on all-eight and twisted-holonomy instances first; compute jets of every affine-fiber point, span them, and search the full mixed code for zero-jet illegal words.

**Likely death.** Three legal jets still XOR cheaply, or logarithmic-degree splitter coverage becomes quasipolynomial.

### 5. Splitter-isolated witness sectors with coded selectors
**Core/expected move.** Use a deterministic perfect-hash family on triple coordinates. In sector \(h\), an injectively colored matching hits the fixed “all colors once” syndrome; couple sector-choice columns through a BCH selector code so superpositions of different sectors should pay selector distance rather than entering one common legal affine class.

**Map check.** O1: hashes are global, not local polynomial signatures. O2: the selector is a dangerous affine branch interface, so O2 may apply unless the complete syndrome fiber defeats rectangle splices. O3: no local scopes; odd holonomy can mix sectors. O4: no phase completeness assumption. O5: binary rather than integer fibers. O6: polynomial splitter sectors, not assignment columns. O7: no tensor claim; later amplification would still need a compressor. O8: binary transfer is immediate, with selector weight included in the YES baseline.

**Falsification/experiment.** For every \(q=3,m=8\) matching, build the smallest pairwise-perfect hash family, explicit BCH selector columns, and fixed target. Enumerate the full fiber on YES/NO, affine-closure, all-eight, and holonomy dictionaries.

**Likely death.** A three-sector XOR or rectangle splice costs at most a constant multiple of one legal sector; selector baseline erases any gain.

### 6. Multiplicity Reed–Solomon detour
**Core/expected move.** Rebuild exact cover as global interpolation: a candidate matching determines a low-degree polynomial through selected labeled points, while multiplicity evaluations include Hasse derivatives. A NO instance should require many derivative disagreements by a root-count bound; extension-field symbols are then binary-expanded with a constant-weight linear inner code.

**Map check.** O1: genuinely global polynomial evaluation, not a Boolean local signature. O2: no marginals or gate transcript. O3: no scope hierarchy; holonomy is replaced by one global polynomial. O4: no phases. O5: no integer slacks. O6: evaluation columns are polynomially many and do not enumerate assignments. O7: no tensor compression; arbitrary combinations are governed by linear-code distance/list-recovery instead. O8: binary expansion must preserve symbol cost uniformly; then exact transfer applies with the full inner-block rank.

**Falsification/experiment.** For \(q=3,4\), encode triples as field points, enumerate all degree bounds and multiplicities \(s\le3\), and compute exact YES/NO binary distances, including all-eight and holonomy-derived dictionaries.

**Likely death.** Interpolation only converts \(q\) versus \(q+2\) into another additive gap, or binary inner encoding flattens multiplicity information.

### 7. Low-degree symmetric-group Fourier shell
**Core/expected move.** Starting from the variable pair-projection construction, lift each projection table into selected Specht-module matrix coefficients of \(S_q\), linearized directly through degree-\(d\) table monomials. Normalize representation blocks so every genuine permutation has small common cost, while signed nonpermutation tables should violate many irreducible identities without paying the \(q\)-sized table baseline.

**Map check.** O1: fixed \(d\) remains vulnerable to bounded-degree cube relations; only growing-degree or globally compressed Specht blocks escape. O2: direct monomial rows avoid circuit tableaux. O3: no scopes, but odd holonomy may satisfy low-degree identities. O4: not a phase lift. O5: fixed-degree uniqueness remains within the bounded-degree exact-fiber obstruction; this is an honest unresolved collision. O6: table monomials, not assignment fingerprints, though count \(q^{O(d)}\). O7: representation products are not sufficient unless every mixed word is checked. O8: after binary realization, transfer is exact; legal block norm and rank must be included.

**Falsification/experiment.** At \(q=3,4\), add all Specht blocks through \(d=3\) to `verify_variable_pair_projection_cvp.py`; exhaust signed coefficients and all support-three trades.

**Likely death.** Affine combinations of three permutations remain constant-cost, while degree needed for separation makes the monomial dictionary superpolynomial.
